item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is materially closer to the frozen contract: it exposes the exact required Upload signature, retains FilesOption behavior, and reuses multipartbody.NewFile. B replaces the required option type, adds expressly forbidden association APIs, and broadens multipart and retry machinery unnecessarily.","reasons":["A implements Upload(ctx, fileName, content, opts ...FilesOption) exactly; B instead uses ...AddFileOption, so the contracted API is absent and existing FilesOption values cannot be used.","B adds multiple public association options and multipart fields despite the explicit prohibition on adding association fields.","A reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile directly, while B introduces NewFileWithFields and sorting machinery solely to support its out-of-contract fields.","A provides stronger relevant verification: multipart field/name/content, Upload retry, validation, open-file input, and lower-level Add retry. B does not directly test Upload retry behavior or source-reader failures."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add's request construction, decoding, and error handling by calling Raw.Do directly instead of routing through FilesService.Add as required.","The RawClient seekable-body changes are broader than the requested Upload implementation and alter ownership and retry behavior globally.","Neither added Upload test covers a failing source reader. The seekable wiring also shares one ReadSeeker across GetBody calls, which is less robust than the established buffered multipart path."],"risks_b":["Upload has the wrong public signature and introduces a parallel option system, violating the exact API contract and FilesOption compatibility.","It adds forbidden association fields and unrelated multipart helper complexity.","Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates its request/response logic instead of preserving one implementation path before Raw.Do handling request body; on an io.ReadAll error, makeBodyReplayable silently returns after partially consuming the body, potentially sending truncated data instead of propagating the reader failure. It also buffers every non-replayable RawClient body globally, an unnecessary behavior and memory-use expansion."]}
